title: Hot Dog Sandwich, NFS, on Wheat Bread

content.title: About
content.content: A hot‑dog sandwich is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a grilled or boiled sausage placed inside a split wheat bun. The NFS (No Fillings & Sauces) version means no extra sauces or toppings, highlighting the flavor of the sausage and the bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first hot‑dog appeared in the United States in the late 19th century and quickly became popular with railway passengers.
Wheat buns used for classic hot‑dogs are usually soft with a slightly crisp crust after a quick toast.
NFS sausages are often made from beef, pork, or a blend, without artificial fillers.
In some countries hot‑dogs are served with sauerkraut, but the NFS version excludes such additions.
International Hot‑Dog Day is celebrated on July 23.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The sausage provides about 12 g of protein per 100 g, helping maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef and pork sausages are rich in heme iron, which supports oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: A hot‑dog delivers quick calories, useful during periods of high physical activity.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Sausages contain niacin, vitamin B12, and riboflavin, supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Carbohydrates from bread
items.content: The wheat bun supplies glucose, the brain’s primary energy source.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Sausages are often salty; excess sodium can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Traditional sausages contain saturated fats, which may contribute to cardiovascular disease when consumed frequently.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have allergic reactions to meat proteins or added preservatives.

items.title: Additives and preservatives
items.content: Certain recipes use glutamates or other additives that can cause sensitivity in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hot‑dogs are typically eaten by hand, holding the bun so the sausage stays in place. Optional condiments like mustard, ketchup, or pickles can be added, but they are omitted in the NFS version.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sausages in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C, and keep a prepared sandwich no longer than 2 hours at room temperature. Keep the bread in a sealed bag in a dry place to prevent it from drying out.
